headline: Kindness is contagious—a single act can ripple through three degrees of separation
universal_truth: Every act of kindness matters more than we can see
fun_facts: Research shows that witnessing kindness makes people more likely to be kind—the 'elevation effect'
A single act of kindness can ripple through social networks, affecting strangers you'll never meet
Being kind releases oxytocin, serotonin, and dopamine—making both giver and receiver feel better
discussion_questions: When has a stranger's kindness changed your day?
What small act of kindness do you still remember years later?
How might your kindness today affect someone you'll never know?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A stranger holds the door for you. It costs them two seconds. But something shifts in you—and maybe you hold the door for the next person. That small kindness just started a chain reaction. Today, we follow where kindness travels.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Scientists have mapped how emotions spread through social networks. Happiness ripples. Sadness ripples. But kindness? It has a special property that makes it spread even further.

options.text: Witnessing kindness inspires others to be kind
options.response: Exactly. It's called moral elevation—seeing goodness makes us want to create more of it.

options.text: People return kindness to the person who gave it
options.response: That happens too, but kindness spreads even beyond direct reciprocation...

q1.title: The Elevation Effect
q1.script: Psychologist Jonathan Haidt discovered that witnessing acts of kindness creates a warm, uplifting feeling he calls 'elevation.' This emotional state makes people more likely to help others. Kindness is literally contagious—like a positive virus spreading through society.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Elevation Effect"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Three Degrees of Influence
q2.script: Research by Nicholas Christakis shows that behaviors ripple through three degrees of social connection. Your kindness affects your friends, your friends' friends, and even your friends' friends' friends. Most of your impact is invisible to you.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Helper's High
q3.script: Being kind isn't just good for others—it's good chemistry. Acts of kindness release oxytocin, serotonin, and dopamine. Your brain rewards you for being generous. Evolution built kindness into our reward system.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You'll never know the full extent of your kindness. That encouragement you gave once might have saved someone's life. The ripples of good we create travel far beyond our sight.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 9. Tomorrow, we'll master the lost art of really listening. Until then, do one kind thing for someone—and trust the ripple.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Ripple Effect - Secret Kindness
growTrack.learning_objective: Create a positive ripple effect through anonymous kindness
growTrack.activity: Do one anonymous act of kindness today—pay for someone's coffee, leave an encouraging note, or help without expecting thanks. Feel the reward without the recognition.
